candidate.answerReason: Updating the tile count gives 18 operations before it first reaches 1. Structurally, each square count k² reaches (k−1)² in exactly two operations, so 10² reaches 1² in 18 operations.

methods.label: Track the number of tiles
methods.explanation:
Renumbering means that only the current number of tiles matters. If there are \(N\) tiles and \(k^2\) is the largest perfect square no greater than \(N\), then the square labels are exactly \(1^2,2^2,\ldots,k^2\). The operation removes \(k\) tiles, leaving \(N-k\).

For example, \(100\) tiles lose \(10\) tiles, leaving \(90\). Since \(9^2\le90<10^2\), the next operation removes \(9\), leaving \(81\). Applying the same rule throughout gives
\[
100\to90\to81\to72\to64\to56\to49,
\]
\[
49\to42\to36\to30\to25\to20\to16,
\]
\[
16\to12\to9\to6\to4\to2\to1.
\]
Each arrow represents one operation. There are six arrows in each row, for \(18\) operations altogether. Every earlier count exceeds \(1\), so we stop after exactly \(18\) operations, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: The method requires only counting positive square labels and performing successive integer subtractions.

methods.label: Group operations between consecutive squares
methods.explanation:
Look at what happens when the tile count is a perfect square. With \(k^2\) tiles, where \(k\ge2\) is an integer, there are exactly \(k\) square labels. One operation therefore leaves \(k^2-k\) tiles.

This new count lies strictly between \((k-1)^2\) and \(k^2\), because
\[
k^2-k-(k-1)^2=k-1>0
\]
and \(k^2-k<k^2\). Thus its square labels are exactly \(1^2,2^2,\ldots,(k-1)^2\). The next operation removes \(k-1\) tiles and leaves
\[
k^2-k-(k-1)=(k-1)^2.
\]
So the pattern
\[
k^2\longrightarrow k^2-k\longrightarrow(k-1)^2
\]
always takes exactly two operations.

Starting at \(100=10^2\), we pass through the squares with roots \(10,9,\ldots,1\). There are nine decreases of the root, each requiring two operations. No intermediate count is \(1\), since \(k^2-k\ge2\) for \(k\ge2\). Hence the first arrival at one tile occurs after \(2\cdot9=18\) operations, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
